stem: Bilal has two identical-looking iron rods, P and Q. One may be a magnet and the other a plain iron rod. A paper sticker marked M is stuck on rod P. He also has a known bar magnet with clear North and South poles.

parts.text: How can he tell which rod is a magnet?

options.text: Find which rod is repelled by one pole of the known magnet.
Find which rod is attracted by the known magnet.
Choose the M-labelled rod as the magnet.
Expect both ends of a magnetised rod to be attracted by the North pole of the known magnet.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Only another magnet can be repelled. A plain iron rod is attracted by both poles, so attraction alone cannot identify a magnet.

teacher.key_rationale: Repulsion between like poles identifies a magnet. Attraction happens with plain iron too. Picking a rod first is not a magnetic test. Both ends of a magnet are not attracted by one North pole.
